learning_outcomes.text: Understand the architecture of modern operating systems (monolithic, modular, microkernel, distributed).
Describe the lifecycle of a process and the role of threads and system calls.
Analyze scheduling strategies, memory management, and synchronization mechanisms.
Understand the structure and functioning of filesystems and virtual memory.
Recognize key mechanisms of interaction between kernel and user space.
Use the Bash shell to run system commands, process text data, and automate tasks.
Develop complete Bash scripts using variables, control structures, and advanced commands.
Administer a Unix-like system: user management, permissions, processes, services, and software packages.
Monitor system status and troubleshoot issues using appropriate tools.
Use networking tools for remote interaction and diagnostics (ssh, ping, curl, etc.).

syllabus_topics: Overview of operating systems (monolithic, modular, microkernel, distributed architecture)
Compilation process, symbols, linking, and libraries
Synchronization primitives (semaphores, mutexes, shared memory, pipes, sockets, signals)
System memory (segmentation, paging, virtual memory, hardware support)
Introduction to the command line and bash
Basic commands (man, cd, ls, echo, su, sudo ...)
Filesystem interaction (mkdir, pwd, find, chown, chmod, ...)
Text input processing (grep, awk, sed, cut, cat, ...)
Scripting (variables, data types, operations, if statements, loops, tests, ...)
Software package management – focus on apt
teaching_methods: Practical exercises in the lab or in an equipped classroom (students are required to use their own laptop)

assessment_methods.method: Written exam to assess theoretical knowledge, consisting of both multiple-choice and open-ended questions
Lab exam focused on developing Bash scripts that incorporate the commands covered in class

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as the arithmetic mean of the two exam scores. Both exams must be passed within 150 days.
bibliography: Operating System concepts (A. Silberschats, P.B. Galvin, G. Gagne)
institution: Università degli Studi di Modena e Reggio Emilia — Ingegneria Informatica (MO)
